title: DROP TRIGGER
description: Learn how to remove triggers using the DROP TRIGGER statement.

data.text: The DROP TRIGGER statement removes one or more triggers from the database. Use the IF EXISTS option to avoid errors when dropping a trigger that may not exist.

data.title: DROP TRIGGER for DML triggers
data.content: Drops a DML trigger safely if it exists.

data.title: DROP TRIGGER for DDL triggers
data.content: Drops a DDL trigger with DATABASE or ALL SERVER scope.
data.code:
DROP TRIGGER [IF EXISTS] trigger_name [, ...n]
ON { DATABASE | ALL SERVER };

data.title: DROP TRIGGER Key Points
points: Use DROP TRIGGER to remove triggers from the database.
Always use IF EXISTS to avoid errors on non-existent triggers.
Dropping a table automatically removes all associated triggers.
DDL triggers require the ON DATABASE or ALL SERVER clause.
